summits_covered.name: CM Mamata Banerjee overseas investment roadshows (UK, Singapore, Spain, Italy, Germany, UAE) - various

method: WebSearch + WebFetch across official BGBS site (bengalglobalsummit.com), WBIDC, Indian and international business press (Business Standard, Deccan Herald, Economic Times-linked wires, PTI/Wire syndications, sector trade press e.g. DataCenterDynamics/w.media for data centres, se.com/company press releases), Wikipedia (Bengal Silicon Valley Tech Hub, List of data centres in West Bengal, Economy of West Bengal) as a company-name index to then verify independently, and direct fetch of individual company press releases where reachable. IMPORTANT FINDING: coverage of BGBS 2022/2023/2025 is overwhelmingly aggregate (total MoU counts: 86 in 2019, 137 in 2022, 188 in 2023, 212 in 2025; total proposed investment in lakh-crore figures) and dominated by named INDIAN conglomerates (Reliance, ITC, JSW, Adani, RP-Sanjiv Goenka, Ambuja Neotia, Birla, TCG/Chatterjee Group, Emami). Individually-named FOREIGN company MoUs are rarely disclosed in press coverage of the summits themselves - most verified foreign-company entries below were found instead via sector/trade press (data centres, semiconductors, industrial capex press releases) covering real government-facilitated land/investment agreements in the same 2021-2026 window, rather than from a BGBS ceremony MoU list, and this distinction is flagged per-entry below. No official BGBS MoU signatory list or PDF naming individual companies was found publicly.

mous.proposed_investment: Rs 2,000 crore (~US$241.5m) planned for the Kolkata campus per Feb 2023 reporting, part of NTT's broader ~US$2.5bn India investment plan; Phase 1 outlay reported as ~Rs 500 crore
mous.summit_or_event: Not confirmed as a Bengal Global Business Summit ceremony MoU - this is a land purchase (7.5 acres, Feb 2023) and Bhumi Pujan groundbreaking in the state government's Bengal Silicon Valley Tech Hub (New Town, WBHIDCO-controlled IT park)
mous.mou_date: 2023-02-13 (land purchase/groundbreaking reported); land allocation within Bengal Silicon Valley Tech Hub occurred 2022 per secondary sourcing

mous.company: ST Telemedia Global Data Centres India (STT GDC India)
mous.country_of_headquarters: Singapore (ST Telemedia Global Data Centres is majority-owned by Singapore Technologies Telemedia; not explicitly restated in the fetched India-specific source, so flagged MEDIUM-HIGH rather than HIGH)
mous.proposed_investment: INR 450 crore for the New Town, Kolkata (STT Kolkata 2) campus
mous.summit_or_event: Not confirmed as a BGBS ceremony MoU - facility launch/inauguration in New Town, Kolkata (Bengal Silicon Valley Tech Hub)

mous.sector: Semiconductors - fabless design, test, and power-electronics R&D centre
mous.proposed_investment: Not disclosed (facility: cleanroom + chip packaging line + design-test labs at STPI Salt Lake Sector V, ~13,000 sq ft acquired with an additional ~19,000 sq ft requested)
mous.summit_or_event: Announced via meetings between GlobalFoundries, West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, and US Consul General Kathy Giles-Diaz; space allocated by West Bengal Government/STPI - not confirmed as a BGBS ceremony MoU

mous.sector: Electrical equipment manufacturing - Vacuum Interrupters (power systems)
mous.summit_or_event: Independent groundbreaking/foundation-laying ceremony at Prospace Industrial Park, Kolkata - not confirmed as tied to a Bengal Global Business Summit MoU
mous.follow_through_status: no follow-up news found (planned completion was reported as Feb 2024 with production targeted Q2 FY24-25; no independent confirmation found that the plant is now operational)

mous.proposed_investment: ~Rs 100 crore (reported capacity-expansion figure for the Haldia port-based refinery; this is incremental capex on an existing JV plant, not a new-entrant MoU)
mous.summit_or_event: Not tied to a specific named summit in sourcing found; general West Bengal industrial investment reporting
mous.mou_date: Exact date not independently confirmed (reporting reviewed clustered around 2022)

mous.company: Bata India (Bata Shoe Organisation / Bata Brands SA parent)
mous.country_of_headquarters: Switzerland (Bata Shoe Organisation, Lausanne) - Bata India Ltd is majority-owned by the Swiss-headquartered Bata group
mous.proposed_investment: Rs 30 crore (Rs 300 million) - manufacturing-technology upgrade, not a new plant
mous.summit_or_event: Independent company capex announcement at its existing Batanagar, West Bengal factory - not a state-government MoU or summit-linked commitment
mous.follow_through_status: operational (technology upgrade to an existing running factory, not a greenfield commitment)

negative_notes: Aggregate BGBS totals by year (context only, not attributable to named foreign companies): 2019 - 86 MoUs, ~Rs 2.84 lakh crore proposed (outside the 2021-2026 window, included for trend context only); 2022 - 137 MoUs/LoIs/EoIs, ~Rs 3.42-3.76 lakh crore depending on source; 2023 - 188 MoUs, Rs 3,76,288 crore; 2025 - 212 MoUs/LoIs, Rs 4.40 lakh crore (some wire coverage cites Rs 91,000 crore as a narrower 'firm commitments' figure). None of the sources reviewed published a full itemised MoU signatory list.

BGBS 2022 partner-country delegations (Japan, Italy, Netherlands, UK, South Korea, US, Australia, New Zealand, Vietnam, Finland, Morocco, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Kenya) were reported as making country-level statements of interest (e.g. 'Japan and Italy want to invest in MSME sector') with NO individual company named or investment figure attached - excluded per task rules against uncritically repeating unverified summit rhetoric.

BGBS 2023 partner countries included Australia, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Fiji, France, Germany, Japan, Kenya, Luxembourg, Malaysia, Nepal, Netherlands, Poland, Rwanda, Slovak Republic, South Korea, and UK (17 countries, ~400 international delegates) - no company-level MoU breakdown by nationality was found in press coverage reviewed.

Mitsubishi Chemical Group - held exploratory talks with West Bengal government (Durgapur/Panagarh sites) re: a possible semiconductor supply-chain investment; as of the most recent reporting found (mid-2026), this remains preliminary discussion with NO MoU signed, no investment figure, and no timeline disclosed. Excluded from the verified list per instructions not to include unconfirmed proposals.

The Bengal government signed an MoU with Spain's La Liga (football league) to set up a football academy during one of CM Mamata Banerjee's overseas trips - this is a sports/cultural partnership, not a commercial investment/JV, so excluded as out of scope.

CM Mamata Banerjee's overseas roadshows (UK, Singapore in 2023; Italy/Germany in 2023 - visited Munich among other German cities with a business delegation, hosted by BVMW and the German Chambers of Commerce (IHK); Spain, Dubai/UAE legs also reported) were described in press as securing unspecified 'major MoUs' - no individually named foreign companies or investment figures were found for these legs despite targeted searching, so none are included.

Haldia Petrochemicals Ltd (HPL) - The Chatterjee Group (TCG), HPL's largest private shareholder, is US-based (Purnendu Chatterjee), but TCG/HPL's relationship with West Bengal dates to the 1980s-90s (pre-window) and its 'foreign' character is ambiguous (Indian-origin founder, long-standing joint promoter with the West Bengal government itself). A ~Rs 8,500 crore polycarbonate plant was reported as being 'explored' by HPL in March 2025, but no signed MoU or firm date was found. Excluded as ambiguous/unconfirmed.

Ricoh India (Japan-origin) appears in a West Bengal data-centre list (SALTLEC facility, marked operational) but this facility appears to predate the 2021-2026 window and no new MoU or investment event within the window was found for it - excluded.

Extensive searches for other plausible foreign investors in West Bengal in this window (Siemens, Bosch, ABB, DP World, Maersk/APM Terminals, PepsiCo, Coca-Cola, Cargill, Kansai Nerolac, Asian Paints/Jotun, Suzuki, Toyota, Samsung, LG, DBS/HSBC/Standard Chartered/Citibank, Capgemini/Cognizant/Tech Mahindra land parcels in Bengal Silicon Valley) turned up either no West Bengal-specific investment news in this window, or land/office allocations without a confirmed investment figure or signing date precise enough to verify individually - none met the bar for inclusion.

No official, itemised, government-published MoU signatory list for any BGBS edition (2022, 2023, or 2025) could be located publicly - WBIDC's own summit page and the bengalglobalsummit.com overview pages describe the event format but do not name signatories. This opacity is itself consistent with the 'MoU graveyard' phenomenon the task describes: verifiable, individually-named foreign-company commitments are the exception in public reporting, not the rule.
